name: NWWA World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own top belt, portrayed under real WWF names at every turn the surviving record captures it: the Rock lost it to Buff Tortoise in a ladder match at the 30 May 1999 “Slamfest,” regained it by an unrecorded route before the 29 August 1999 “Fall Classic: War Games” (where he retained against Kirk with Chris Jericho's help), and Hellwolf was defending it by the 25 June 2000 “Slamfest” — a second title change the record also never shows. The fed's own dedicated title-history page, dated 2 July 2000, lists it Vacant, a blank template never updated to match its own pay-per-view results.

name: NWWA International Championship
epitaph: Named inconsistently by the fed's own hand — "International" on its dedicated title-history page and in the 25 June 2000 "Slamfest" script that crowned Gorilla its new champion, "Intercontinental" in the two 1999 pay-per-views that billed Kirk as its holder. Both readings are recorded rather than picking one. How and when Kirk's own reign ended and the title was declared vacant before Gorilla's win is likewise not in the surviving record.

name: NWWA National Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Billed the “United States Title” in the one pay-per-view script that shows it defended — Buff Bagwell retaining against Dale Hill at the 30 May 1999 “Slamfest” — against the “National Heavyweight” name its own dedicated (and otherwise blank) title-history page carries. The surviving record never shows how Bagwell became champion; his reign is registered from the earliest point he is shown holding the title.

name: NWWA Internet Championship
epitaph: The one title whose own dedicated history page was actually filled in: Scott Credible, crowned its first champion in a six-man battle royal at the 25 June 2000 "Slamfest." The same card's own script separately bills a Killerwolf-vs.-Scott Durden ladder match for the same belt, a contradiction the fed's own text never resolves.

name: NWWA Hardcore Championship
epitaph: Listed on the fed's own roster of six championships; its own dedicated title-history page is a blank, never-filled template, and no reign for it survives anywhere in the captured record.

name: NWWA Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Triple H is billed “one half of the NWWA Tag Team Champions” at the 29 August 1999 “Fall Classic: War Games” — the only trace of this title anywhere in the surviving record. His reign is registered from that earliest, and only, point the record shows him holding it, with neither his partner's name nor how the team won the belt ever recorded.

name: NWWA Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Listed on the fed's own roster of six championships, restricted by its own rules to wrestlers under 230 pounds. Its own dedicated title-history page is a blank, never-filled template, and no reign for it survives anywhere in the captured record.
